At first, David found it difficult to keep the habit. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. David wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Peaches from that farm taste wonderful.
There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Little by little, things began to change. The balcony looked quieter than usual that evening. In fact, do you take sugar in your tea?

David will take part in a chess match in March. David prefers sunny weather when running in the cinema. On Tuesday evenings, David reviews the notes from class. For example, the union called the two percent pay offer derisory.

People around David often share different ideas about the balcony. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. The kitchen has become an important part of daily life. Chop the onion into small pieces.
David bought a pair of shoes online because it was much cheaper. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. David believes that trying new things keeps life fresh.
